priorStories.headline: U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate
priorStories.body:
The U.S. economy expanded at an annualized 3.4% in the third quarter, according to the government’s initial estimate, accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter.

Inflation remained elevated in September. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.6% from a year earlier, while the measure excluding food and energy rose 3.1%. Both reports are subject to revision.

priorStories.headline: Israeli election leaves no bloc a majority
priorStories.body:
Israel’s completed vote count gave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority. The main opposition won 48 seats, and Arab-led parties won 19.

The results remain subject to certification and submission to President Isaac Herzog, leaving the next government unresolved.

priorStories.headline: U.S. completes 172-million-barrel oil release
priorStories.body:
The Energy Department awarded contracts to exchange more than 40 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, completing a planned 172-million-barrel emergency release.

The contracts require more than 216 million barrels to be returned to the reserve beginning in 2027.

candidates.summary: Russian and Ukrainian officials participating in a humanitarian mission entered Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine. Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said the convoy was bringing food, medical supplies and other aid to residents under a localized ceasefire.
candidates.title: Humanitarian mission enters Russian-occupied Oleshky

candidates.summary: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran as part of U.S.-coordinated efforts to negotiate an agreement between Iran and the United States, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters. The sides remained divided over whether nuclear issues or an end to the U.S. port blockade and oil sanctions should come first.
candidates.title: Qatari mediators return to Tehran for U.S.-Iran talks

candidates.summary: Meta, TikTok and X lost legal challenges to information demands issued by British online-safety regulator Ofcom. The High Court ruled that the demands, which seek data about platforms’ moderation of harmful content, were lawful under the Online Safety Act.
candidates.title: Meta, TikTok and X lose UK challenge to Ofcom data demands

candidates.summary: The euro-area economy expanded 0.4% in the third quarter from the previous quarter, slowing from 0.6% but exceeding economists’ expectations of 0.2%, according to Eurostat’s preliminary estimate. Output across the 21 countries using the euro was 1.3% higher than a year earlier.
candidates.title: Euro-area economy grows 0.4% in third quarter

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump decided to hold campaign rallies in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday after the appearances had initially been canceled. The events were announced days before the U.S. midterm elections.
candidates.title: Trump restores Iowa and Kansas campaign rallies

candidates.summary: A South African court allowed anti-illegal-immigration groups to hold demonstrations in Durban under restrictions imposed to reduce the risk of violence. Police had asked the court to prohibit the marches following unrest connected to a ruling concerning asylum seekers.
candidates.title: South African court permits Durban immigration marches with restrictions

candidates.summary: The U.S. State Department approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missile interceptors to Ukraine. Funding is to come from Ukraine, Canada, Germany and Norway through the U.S. JUMPSTART program and from European Union-backed financing. The approval does not mean immediate delivery.
candidates.title: U.S. approves possible $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine

candidates.summary: Russia and the United States vetoed each other's proposed U.N. Security Council resolutions concerning Western Sahara. The votes left the U.N. peacekeeping mission without a renewed mandate one day before its expiration and reflected disagreement over whether Morocco's autonomy proposal should be the sole basis for negotiations.
candidates.title: U.S. and Russia veto rival Western Sahara resolutions

candidates.summary: Tens of thousands of students and workers demonstrated across Italy during a 24-hour general strike called by the USB union. Protesters sought higher wages and stronger public services and opposed rising living costs and military spending. Most events were peaceful, though police used water cannons during confrontations in Turin and Rome.
candidates.title: Nationwide strike brings mass demonstrations across Italy

candidates.summary: A divided 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals declined to stop California from counting mail ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters whose citizenship the Justice Department questioned. The majority said granting the administration's request while litigation continued risked disenfranchising eligible voters.
candidates.title: Appeals court declines to block disputed California ballots

candidates.summary: OpenAI announced safeguards that will restrict weapons-related information provided to users identified as teenagers, even absent apparent violent intent. ChatGPT will also be able to end conversations showing fixation on violence, and repeated incidents may prompt temporary account pauses. OpenAI said the measures would begin rolling out over the following weeks.
candidates.title: OpenAI announces tighter violence safeguards for teen ChatGPT users

candidates.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,852 U.S. measles cases through October 29, an increase of 264 from its previous update. The agency listed 511 hospitalizations and three confirmed measles-associated deaths. Unvaccinated people and those whose vaccination status was unknown accounted for 96% of cases.
candidates.title: CDC reports 4,852 U.S. measles cases

candidates.summary: Syrian authorities reported that flash floods caused by torrential rain had killed seven people, including five children, and injured seven others. Four people remained missing. Flooding affected Raqqa, Deir al-Zor, Hasakah and parts of Aleppo, damaging infrastructure, closing roads and displacing families.
candidates.title: Eastern Syria floods leave seven dead

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks closed sharply lower as concerns about technology companies' artificial-intelligence spending deepened. The S&P 500 fell 1.8%, the Nasdaq Composite declined 2.9% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.1%. Intel and Reddit each fell about 29%, while Sandisk dropped about 13%.
candidates.title: Technology selloff drives sharp decline in U.S. stocks

candidates.summary: Meta settled with a teenage plaintiff who alleged that Instagram and Facebook were designed to encourage compulsive use and contributed to mental-health and eating problems. Terms were not disclosed. A planned Los Angeles trial was expected to continue against Snapchat parent Snap after Meta settled with both teen plaintiffs.
candidates.title: Meta settles teen social-media addiction lawsuit

candidates.summary: Russia vetoed a U.S.-drafted Security Council resolution that would have altered the U.N. mission in Western Sahara and made Morocco's autonomy proposal the basis for negotiations. A Russian draft extending the mission for one year then failed with three votes in favor, one against and 11 abstentions, leaving the mandate set to expire October 31.
candidates.title: Rival Western Sahara resolutions fail at U.N. Security Council

candidates.summary: A federal judge temporarily ordered the Justice Department to stop threatening state and local election officials with prosecution for rejecting administration demands concerning alleged noncitizen voters. The order also barred demands to remove listed voters, reject their ballots or segregate their ballots during the midterm elections.
candidates.title: Judge restricts Justice Department demands on election officials

candidates.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration began issuing federal registrations to more than 900 state-licensed medical-marijuana dispensaries in Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, South Dakota, Texas, Virginia and West Virginia. The registrations implement federal Schedule III controls for qualifying medical-marijuana activities and subject recipients to federal security, recordkeeping and inventory requirements.
candidates.title: DEA begins registering more than 900 medical-marijuana dispensaries

candidates.summary: Canada and the European Union launched an “Alliance for the Future” covering trade, technology, critical resources, security and other areas. They concluded substantive negotiations on a digital-trade agreement and agreed to define by their 2027 summit a closer association short of full EU membership; no associate-membership agreement was finalized.
candidates.title: Canada and EU launch broader alliance and conclude digital-trade talks

candidates.summary: A federal judge ordered the government to remove three taxpayer-funded Trump administration advertisements from official websites and social media and cancel authorized third-party distribution while litigation continues. The judge found the challengers were likely to succeed in arguing that the ads were political or propaganda material funded without congressional authorization.
candidates.title: Judge orders removal of three taxpayer-funded administration ads

candidates.summary: Binance said it was working with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in assets affected by an estimated $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft disclosed the previous day. The exchange said Friday that it was beginning efforts to recover money for users; blockchain intelligence firm TRM assessed that a North Korean hacking unit was probably responsible.
candidates.title: Binance says roughly $3 billion frozen after cryptocurrency theft

candidates.summary: A U.S. official and a coalition of veterans and advocacy groups said the Trump administration planned to deport some Afghan immigrants to Afghanistan through Pakistan. The Department of Homeland Security declined to confirm prospective removal operations, and the reported deportations had not occurred by the end of the target day.
candidates.title: Trump administration plans deportations of some Afghan immigrants
